answer: Here is one mechanism that works: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because jade only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, meadow is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any sable approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
